title: Going to New York to join Wingy Manone in 1938-39
summary: With Ray Benitez, he took the train to New York at New Year's, stayed with Sharky, and Benitez could not get union work.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: the record with them. But I don't know. Well tell me about John and Wingy. Did you leave from here to John and Wingy or what? How did that work? Yeah, I'd come home. Well I'd been

home, let's see, well I came home in 36, you see, and I played with Curse for a while. And then it was around the end of 38 and Wingy sent for me. And I got to know Ray Benitez around here, we used to hang around together at night and time. And Wingy sent for both of us. And Ray was tickled to death because he wanted to get to New York, but he didn't have a New York car and he thought he could get in, but he couldn't make it, couldn't get in. For me they said they sent him back? No, he stayed up there for a while. But he wouldn't let him play? No, he couldn't get in the union. You know, he wouldn't try to. How come? Well, he couldn't get in or something. He couldn't join the union and go right on a job, you know. You had to have a transfer period. You had to have a transfer period six months before you could take a job, it seemed like at that time. Well he didn't stay all that time, did you? Well he put his car in, but he didn't stay that long. He stayed up there when Sharky was up there. We lived together for a while up there. I was up there about three months with Sharky before we came back there. That's about all three or four months. So Ray never did get to play all the time. No, he never did get to play. Well you could play spots and stuff. Oh yeah, you could play spots, yeah, but you couldn't take a...
Well he probably played a few spots out there. No, Ray probably played some job, I don't

recall, but I guess he did. He used to hang around with Goodman's brother. Ray got to be pretty pretty good friend with him. The bass player? The trumpet player. Freddie. Freddie, yeah, Freddie. Ray used to come
to the park a long time. Well you left on the train together with him?

Yeah, yeah, we left on the train together. Just the two of you? Yeah. We went up there on the train and we got to New York, I tell you when we got to New York on New Year's Eve night, I think we got to New York, and we moved right in with Sharky because we knew when Sharky was up there, we moved in with him. And that same night, I think it was New Year's Eve we got there, I think. Joe Conduo was a volunteer. I knew him from before. He worked in a club right on 48th Street there, some club, I can't tell you the name, but I forgot it. But I knew, I didn't know him well, but I knew him by name, well, you know, I didn't know him as a volunteer leader. And he invited, Sharky got to know him and they invited Sharky and all of us up to his house. We went up there, man, one of them Italian dinners, everything from octopus on up, you know, chicken, spaghetti, meatballs and all, God. We went up there that night. It was late too, New Year's Eve, we went up there. Somewhere up in the Bronx, we went up there. I remember growing up there with Sharky and all of us, and we really had a big one. All you wanted to eat and drink.
